stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: The AI race is back on
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The AI competitive landscape is intensifying, with Anthropic and OpenAI currently leading the field.
Google and Meta are noted as lagging behind the frontrunners despite significant investment in AI.
The narrative suggests a renewed and highly competitive 'AI race' among major tech players.

stories.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: AI is being leveraged to design novel proteins.
These engineered proteins possess the capability to break down highly stable molecular bonds.
This development has significant implications for fields like drug discovery and materials science.

stories.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Anthropic warns of a new threat where small AI models could self-replicate.
The potential mechanism involves using low-power IoT devices as vectors for these 'replicators'.
This development suggests a significant evolution in computer worm threats driven by AI.

stories.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Researchers discovered vulnerabilities in new AI models from OpenAI and Google.
These flaws allow attackers to trick the models into generating explicit or 'nude' content.
The finding highlights significant security weaknesses in current AI safety guardrails.

stories.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Naoto Yokoya
bullet_points: Proposes a paradigm shift for Earth Observation (EO) by automating the model building process.
Suggests that any EO task can be framed as a verifiable problem for an AI agent (harness/verifier setup).
Aims to move away from manual, expert-driven training recipes toward recursive self-improvement in EO modeling.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Tags confirm its association with major AI frameworks like transformers and the Llama family.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to major AI frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A security breach occurred at OpenAI involving a hidden recording device found in a top-secret meeting room.
An OpenAI engineer is facing serious legal consequences, including a potential 5-year sentence and a $250K fine.
The FBI is pursuing foreign spy charges against the individual involved in the espionage incident.

stories.title: Ukraine blindsided by Starlink throttling restrictions and intelligence gaps
stories.author: Christopher Miller, Financial Times
bullet_points: Ukrainian forces are experiencing connectivity issues while using Starlink.
The problems are attributed to Starlink throttling restrictions and intelligence gaps.
The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities in reliance on private satellite infrastructure during conflict.

stories.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Introduces 'ChunkAct,' a method to improve the efficiency of agentic robotics systems.
Addresses the high computational cost of current LLM-driven robots, which suffer from redundant reasoning over full interaction histories.
Aims to enable LLM agents to generalize to new tasks without constant retraining by optimizing how actions are reasoned about.

stories.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
stories.author: Liang Chen
bullet_points: DoubtLess is a novel, training-free decoding method designed to optimize reasoning models.
It addresses the inefficiency of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting by reducing unnecessary token usage.
The method uses a smaller reasoning model to steer a larger model, avoiding the need for additional training or restrictive heuristics.

stories.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
stories.author: Liang Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'DoubtLess,' a novel training-free decoding method for reasoning models.
Addresses the inefficiency of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, which often generates unnecessary tokens.
Uses a smaller reasoning model to steer a larger model, avoiding the need for additional training or accuracy-sacrificing heuristics.

stories.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Introduces 'ChunkAct,' a method to improve the efficiency of LLM-based agentic robotics.
Addresses the high computational cost in current systems where LLMs re-reason over the entire interaction history for every primitive.
Aims to enable LLM agents to generalize to new tasks without requiring full retraining by optimizing reasoning.

stories.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
stories.author: Liang Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'DoubtLess,' a novel training-free decoding method for reasoning models.
Addresses the inefficiency of long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning by reducing token usage without sacrificing accuracy.
Uses a smaller reasoning model to steer a larger model, avoiding the need for model retraining or fixed steering vectors.

stories.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
stories.author: bleepingcomputer.com via janus
bullet_points: GitLab has issued a warning regarding a critical vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as having maximum severity.
The flaw allows for potential remote code execution (RCE).

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses deployment and safety concerns for running local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports integration with Ollama.
This integration allows users to utilize open-source models through Claude.
Ollama functions as a third-party gateway provider for this functionality.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft collaborated with Japan's National Police Agency to dismantle a large-scale cybercrime network.
The network was responsible for distributing over a billion scam and phishing messages globally.
The operation targets the infrastructure used by scammers to send fraudulent messages like fake parking tickets or package notifications.

stories.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Character.AI is undergoing bankruptcy proceedings.
New York Attorney General Letitia James is leading a multi-state investigation into the company.
The focus of the investigation is ensuring consumer data sold by Character.AI receives proper regulatory protections.

stories.title: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: YouTube is implementing new labeling for music tracks generated or significantly altered by AI.
This initiative mirrors YouTube's existing policy for labeling AI-generated video content.
The labeling will specifically target tracks that are 'altered or fully generated' by AI tools.

stories.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: The study investigates how to effectively incorporate demonstration quality during Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pretraining.
It empirically compares different methods—weighting, filtering, and conditioning—using 5,000 suboptimal human demonstrations across 24 target tasks.
The research examines the impact of pretraining data size and quality tags on downstream fine-tuning and inference performance.

stories.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
stories.author: Yong Jae Lee
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of training long-horizon AI agents capable of autonomous, multi-day tasks.
A key hurdle identified is the scarcity of training data and the difficulty in providing dense feedback for complex, sparse-reward tasks.
The research introduces a method ('Tev') to scale these agentic environments using dense progress rewards to overcome data and reward sparsity issues.

stories.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
stories.author: Chong Luo
bullet_points: AesCode addresses the limitations of current AI models in generating aesthetically pleasing and structured visual artifacts (like slides/dashboards) as code.
The core problem addressed is the gap between code generation (structured but visually blind) and image generation (visually rich but content-unreliable).
The solution introduces a decoupled cross-modal reward system to improve spatial planning and aesthetic quality in code generation.

stories.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
stories.author: James Zou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents' (HybridAgents) to address limitations in current LLM agents.
These agents bridge the gap between efficient, latent internal reasoning and external, text-based interaction.
The core innovation is a unified generation process that dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text interaction.

stories.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
stories.author: Xia Ning
bullet_points: The research addresses multi-objective molecular optimization, a key process in drug discovery.
It focuses on using multi-turn feedback to guide iterative molecular modifications.
The work aims to improve upon existing LLM-based methods that lack explicit training to leverage feedback.

stories.title: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Matthew Tancik
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-RIG, a new benchmark designed to test the robustness of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
The benchmark specifically perturbs only the physical hardware and setup of the robot (e.g., camera mounting, calibration drift, control rates).
It addresses a critical real-world challenge: ensuring robot policies generalize across varied and imperfect deployment environments.

stories.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Shangding Gu
bullet_points: The research explores Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI) for robots, aiming to move beyond human-driven upgrades.
Physical RSI allows real-world physical experience to guide lasting updates to both the robot's capabilities and its learning process.
Key challenges identified for this approach include noisy observations, complex continuous dynamics, and the risk of irreversible errors.

stories.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: The paper investigates how to effectively incorporate demonstration quality during Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pretraining.
It empirically compares different methods—weighting, filtering, and conditioning—using 5,000 suboptimal human demonstrations across 24 tasks.
The study examines the impact of data size and quality tags on VLA performance during both pretraining and fine-tuning.

stories.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
stories.author: Yong Jae Lee
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of training long-horizon autonomous agents, which are crucial for tasks like automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI).
A key bottleneck identified is the scarcity of training data and the sparsity of rewards in complex, long-running tasks.
The proposed solution introduces a method to scale these environments by utilizing 'Dense Progress Rewards' to overcome sparse reward issues.

stories.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
stories.author: James Zou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents' to overcome limitations in current LLM agents.
Addresses the gap between efficient internal 'latent reasoning' and external text-based interaction.
The architecture dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text generation for unified processing.

stories.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
stories.author: Vikas Garg
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of generating graphs whose topological structure exactly matches a target descriptor (Persistence Diagram).
Current topology-aware generative models often rely on soft regularization, leading only to approximate topological similarity.
The paper proposes two principled approaches to achieve exact topological compliance in graph generation.

stories.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
stories.author: Xia Ning
bullet_points: The research addresses multi-objective molecular optimization, a key challenge in drug discovery.
It proposes MFG (Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization) to handle iterative modifications.
The work aims to improve upon existing LLM-based methods that lack explicit training to leverage feedback.

stories.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Shangding Gu
bullet_points: The research proposes 'Physical Recursive Self-Improvement' (Physical RSI) for robots.
Physical RSI aims to allow robots to improve their own capabilities and improvement methods through physical experience.
Key challenges addressed include noisy observations, continuous dynamics, and the high cost of physical trials.

stories.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
stories.author: Yong Jae Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of training long-horizon AI agents for complex, autonomous tasks.
Proposes a solution to sparse reward problems in long-horizon environments using 'Dense Progress Rewards'.
Aims to overcome limitations in current open-source models struggling with complex, multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
stories.author: James Zou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents' to overcome limitations in current LLM agents.
Addresses the gap between efficient internal 'latent reasoning' and external text-based interaction.
The agents dynamically switch between latent reasoning and text generation within a unified process.

stories.title: OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding
stories.author: Lei Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniCompass, a new holistic benchmark designed to evaluate omni-modal video grounding and understanding.
Addresses the limitation of existing benchmarks which only cover partial evaluation dimensions for multimodal LLMs (MLLMs).
Defines two specific evaluation tracks within OmniCompass, including OmniCompass-VL, to systematically diagnose video understanding capabilities.

stories.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
stories.author: Zhihao Lin
bullet_points: The paper addresses the limitations of current LLM temperature sampling methods, which often use fixed or heuristic settings.
It introduces 'Scenario-Actor,' a new, interpretable framework for adapting LLM decoding based on the inferred communicative scenario.
This work aims to move beyond simple global or local calibration to provide a more contextually aware control over LLM randomness.

stories.title: Back-Translation Still Matters: Leveraging Monolingual Data for Low-Resource Machine Translation with LLMs
stories.author: Jitin Singla
bullet_points: The paper investigates leveraging moderate amounts of monolingual data for low-resource machine translation using LLMs.
It proposes that back-translation (BT), a technique from the pre-LLM era, is more effective than continued pretraining for this task.
This offers an alternative strategy to standard few-shot prompting or fine-tuning when parallel data is scarce.

stories.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
stories.author: Yifei Shen
bullet_points: Introduces a 'Self-Evolving Agent Harness' that allows agents to revise their software scaffolding (prompts, memory, workflows) without altering core model weights.
Formalizes a feedback-driven process for persisting accepted revisions across multiple agent runs.
The framework meticulously separates update targets, distinguishing between changes to interpreted state versus revisions to tools, code, and control logic.

stories.title: Banks are now trying to offload the AI data center debt they just underwrote
stories.author: smartmic
bullet_points: Banks are reportedly shifting the financial burden of AI data center infrastructure.
The news highlights a significant financial risk associated with the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.
This indicates a potential shift in how the financial sector manages investments in AI hardware.

stories.title: Memory Isn’t Learning: Why AI Agents Keep Making the Same Mistakes
stories.author: sparsh_jain_ai
bullet_points: The article addresses the limitation of AI agents regarding long-term memory and consistency.
It critiques the current state of AI agents, noting their tendency to repeat past errors.
The core theme is the distinction between 'memory' and 'learning' in current AI architectures.
